title: Fal, OpenAI and Traversal lead a big-round week
lede: Billion-dollar rounds pushed Fal and OpenAI up, Traversal and Applied Compute broke into the 100, and Heidi's layoffs dropped it 53 places. Five companies came in, five went out. A batch of April and October 2025 rounds also aged out of their funding bonus, which moved some scores down half a point.

items.name: Traversal
items.why: A $120M Series B at a $1B valuation (Nov 3) plus 31 open roles.

items.name: OpenAI
items.why: A first close of about $11B at a $1.25T valuation (Nov 6), with the round still open and expected to reach roughly $20B.

items.name: Fal
items.why: A $1.3B Series F led by Bessemer at a $16B valuation, double its April mark (Nov 3).

items.name: Albert Invent
items.why: Open roles grew from 25 to 30, reaching full hiring points.

items.name: Valon
items.why: Open roles grew from 27 to 31, reaching full hiring points.

items.name: Shield AI
items.why: A $1B Series H at a $28.8B valuation, plus a deal to buy Echodyne for $5.3B.

items.name: Cresta
items.why: Salesforce agreed to buy it for a reported $2.7B (Nov 2), its 12th deal of 2026 after Braze ($5.66B), Fin, formerly Intercom ($3.6B), Contentful, Listen Labs, Loops and Rune. Inside Service Cloud, Cresta's voice agents reach every Salesforce service customer. Expected to close February to April 2027; until then it stays on the board.

items.name: Nooks
items.why: A $500M commitment from General Catalyst's Customer Value Fund, revenue-based money paid back from the sales it funds. It isn't equity, so it doesn't count as a round here; the drop is its October 2024 round aging out. Nooks cites 3x growth and 135% net revenue retention.

items.name: Heidi Health
items.why: Open roles fell from 71 to 13 in the same week it cut about 18% of staff and two of its three co-founders announced they are leaving.

sections.heading: The exits
sections.body: Resolve AI (#49), Loop (#72), Lila Sciences (#86), Avoca (#92) and Simile (#98) left the 100. Loop, Lila and Avoca lost half a point as their funding aged; they did not fall because of bad news.

items.why: Right behind Rippling, most likely thanks to last week's feature.

spotlight.label: Featured this week
spotlight.name: Casap
spotlight.tagline: AI agents that run bank payment disputes end to end.

facts.v: Agents handle intake, investigation, evidence, chargebacks, recovery and customer updates. People make the judgment calls.
$56M Series B on Oct 28, 2026, led by Base10 with Experian and Synchrony. $90M raised in total.
More than 100 banks, credit unions, fintechs and processors.
Revenue up 10x since its Series A a year ago.
Fraud, collections, claims and other back-office work.
Win-rate and fraud-loss figures are company-reported.

spotlight.why: When I worked in fintech at Majority, I dealt with the disputes process firsthand. It's complex and very manual: evidence spread across systems, regulatory clocks running, and a call on whether each chargeback is even worth filing. It was obvious it could be automated. Casap does exactly that, using AI to work every dispute and file only the ones worth fighting and likely to win. It reports a 96% chargeback win rate against a 60% industry average, with cases resolved in 8 days instead of up to 90. Now it's using the new money to take on fraud, collections and claims.
